rows.grounds: compound: sṛṣṭi-bāhya-stha-sthūla-sannidhi-yoga-tas; contact with the gross standing outside creation

items.question: How does contact with the gross external world relate to one's own interior?
premises: One's own interior is the locus of experience
The gross stands outside creation
Connection with that gross proximity occurs
items.inference: Awareness moves from the gross external proximity back toward one's own interior.
uncertainties: Exact syntactic role of the compound in the larger sentence is unclear without following verses
items.plain_english: From connection with the gross that stands outside creation, one turns toward one's own interior.

rows.grounds: from the casting of an undeluded vision

items.question: What enables realization of oneness with that from the gross state?
premises: Experience begins from the gross state
An unconfused gaze can be directed
Oneness with that becomes attainable
items.inference: Through an undeluded gaze upon the gross state, one attains oneness with that.
uncertainties: The referent of 'that' depends on the preceding context
items.plain_english: From the gross state, by the fall of an unconfused gaze, one attains oneness with that.

items.question: Where does absorption in rest occur within the fourfold power?
premises: Wherever awareness is directed
Even there rest is possible
Absorption occurs in the fourfold power
items.inference: In any locus whatsoever, absorption in rest is found within the fourfold power.
uncertainties: The specific four powers are not named in this verse
items.plain_english: Wherever it may be, even there what is absorbed in rest abides in the fourfold power.

rows.grounds: by the remedy of contemplating Shiva

items.question: How does contemplation of Shiva affect the mind bound in transmigration?
premises: The mind can be bound in transmigration
Contemplation of Shiva functions as medicine
This medicine acts upon the bound mind
items.inference: When the mind bound in transmigration is held by the medicine of Shiva-contemplation, its bondage is addressed.
uncertainties: The resulting liberation is implied but not explicitly stated in this verse
items.plain_english: When the mind is bound in transmigration, it is held by the medicine of contemplation on Shiva.

rows.grounds: from immersion in the power of each respective principle
possessing a single form across all things

items.question: What realization arises from immersion in the strength of each principle?
premises: Each principle has its own strength
One can enter into that strength
All things can be seen as one form
items.inference: Immersion in the strength of each principle reveals a single form pervading all things.
uncertainties: The grammatical subject experiencing this realization is supplied by context
items.plain_english: From entering the strength of each principle, one realizes that which has one form in all things.

rows.grounds: having brought the senses and so forth under control

items.question: What condition of power becomes firm within one's own body?
premises: Power can be established in one's own body
This power becomes firm
The senses and other faculties come under its control
items.inference: A firm power established in one's own body brings the senses and other faculties under control.
uncertainties: The scope of 'etc.' beyond the senses is not specified
items.plain_english: In one's own body, a firm power arises that has brought the senses and the rest under its control.

items.question: How is Shiva-ness established in the truth of all states?
premises: All states can be engaged in true union
Their truth can be recognized
Shiva-ness abides in that truth
items.inference: Through true union with all states, Shiva-ness is established in their truth.
uncertainties: Whether 'sadyogāt' means sudden union or true union is context-dependent
items.plain_english: Through true union in all states, Shiva-ness is established in their truth.

rows.grounds: the meaning of a word; sandhi: padasya + arthaḥ
the status of being a word-meaning
in the determination or establishment of meaning

items.question: How is the meaning of a word established as word-meaning?
premises: A word has a meaning
That meaning can attain the status of word-meaning
This occurs in the establishment of meaning
items.inference: Thus, in the establishment of meaning, a word's meaning attains the status of word-meaning.
uncertainties: The philosophical criterion for this establishment is not fully stated here
items.plain_english: Thus, in the establishment of meaning, the meaning of a word becomes word-meaning.

rows.grounds: through the absence or non-arising of mind
by having the nature of true form

items.question: What allows abiding in true form everywhere through absence of mind?
premises: Abiding can occur everywhere
Absence of mind is possible
True form can be the mode of abiding
items.inference: Through the absence of mind, abiding everywhere occurs in the nature of true form.
uncertainties: Whether 'cittābhāvena' means cessation or transcendence of mind is interpretive
items.plain_english: Because of abiding everywhere in true form through the absence of mind.

rows.grounds: of everything without exception; sandhi: sarvasya + eva
by the self that is of all forms

items.question: What constitutes the firm form of everything in its all-form nature?
premises: Everything has a form
That form can be firm
The self of all forms underlies it
items.inference: The firm form of everything is grounded in the self that is of all forms.
uncertainties: The compound sarvākāratadātmanā allows slight variation in parsing
items.plain_english: The firm form of everything indeed is by the self that consists of all forms.

rows.grounds: in unity present everywhere; sandhi: sarvatra + aikye
to be generated or brought about
not afflicted by desire and so forth

items.question: What kind of firm establishment arises in unity everywhere free from desire?
premises: Unity can be recognized everywhere
A firm establishment can arise in that unity
This establishment is unstruck by desire and other afflictions
items.inference: In unity everywhere, a firm establishment arises that is unstruck by desire and the rest.
uncertainties: rūḍhiḥ may mean convention or firm realization depending on context
items.plain_english: In unity everywhere, a firm establishment is to be produced, unstruck by desire and the rest.

rows.grounds: immersion in capability or power; sandhi: samarthatā + āveśaḥ

items.question: How are competence and equality distributed between root and middle?
premises: There is a root and a middle
Competence enters at the root
Equality pertains to the middle of these two
items.inference: At the root there is immersion in competence, and in the middle there is equality of these two.
uncertainties: The two referents of etayoḥ are not explicitly named in this verse
items.plain_english: At the root there is entry into competence; in the middle there is equality of these two.

rows.grounds: compound: sarva-amūrta-tva-tattva-āsthā-buddhi-dṛṣṭi-prasakti-tas; from attachment to the intellect's view grounded in the principle of universal formlessness

items.question: What results from attachment to the intellect's view grounded in universal formlessness?
premises: There is a principle of universal formlessness
The intellect can ground its view in that principle
Attachment to that view can arise
items.inference: Attachment to the intellect's view grounded in universal formlessness produces a specific consequence stated in context.
uncertainties: The consequence is carried by the following verse and not explicit here
items.plain_english: From attachment to the intellect's view grounded in the principle of universal formlessness.

rows.grounds: of minds engaged in constructing mine-ness

items.question: How does the mind of the great differ regarding the construction of mine-ness?
premises: Minds can construct mine-ness
There are great ones with a distinct mind
Their mind is characterized exceedingly in some way
items.inference: The mind of the great is exceedingly distinct from minds that construct mine-ness.
uncertainties: The exact predicate completing the comparison is supplied by surrounding verses
items.plain_english: The mind of the great is exceedingly so, compared to minds that construct mine-ness.

rows.grounds: in the mind characterized by mine-ness
having reached the attachment or devotion of the good; two tokens fused in text as given

items.question: What is rightly established in the mind of mine-ness for the good ones?
premises: A mind can be characterized by mine-ness
The good ones can arrive at attachment
This state can be rightly established
items.inference: In the mind of mine-ness, when the attachment of the good ones has arrived, something is rightly established.
uncertainties: The third token contains two words in the source line but is given as one token here
items.plain_english: In the mind of mine-ness, when the attachment of the good ones has arrived, it is well.

rows.grounds: when fully carried out or realized
consisting entirely of that one; sandhi: tadekamayaḥ

items.question: What state arises when the sense that all is mine is fully realized?
premises: One may apprehend all as mine
This apprehension can be fully manifested
A state made of that one can arise
items.inference: When the realization 'all is mine' is fully manifested, a state consisting entirely of that one arises.
uncertainties: The referent of 'that one' depends on the broader doctrinal context
items.plain_english: When 'all is mine' is fully realized, there arises a state made entirely of that one.

rows.grounds: of each individual host of deities

items.question: What follows from fixation of mine-ness toward each group of deities?
premises: There are distinct groups of deities
One can fixate on each as mine
Such fixation has a consequence
items.inference: Fixation of mine-ness toward each group of deities leads to a further development stated in context.
uncertainties: The consequence is completed in the following verse
items.plain_english: From fixation of mine-ness toward each group of deities.

rows.grounds: as a whole or in totality

items.question: How do the spreading powers become undifferentiated and pure collectively?
premises: Powers can spread forth collectively
Differentiation can be removed
They can become pure
items.inference: When spreading forth collectively, they indeed become undifferentiated and pure.
uncertainties: The subject 'they' is inferred from prior verses
items.plain_english: Spreading forth collectively, they indeed become undifferentiated and pure.

rows.grounds: compound: viśeṣa-mamatā-āveśa-praveśa-vaśa-tas; due to entering into immersion in particular mine-ness

items.question: What greatness arises from entering immersion in particular mine-ness?
premises: Particular mine-ness can be entered into
Immersion in it exerts a force
A great state or result arises
items.inference: By the force of entering immersion in particular mine-ness, something great arises.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'great' is context-dependent
items.plain_english: By the force of entering immersion in particular mine-ness, the great arises.

rows.grounds: compound: svaccha-ākāla-kalā-akale; in the pure, timeless, limited, and partless aspects

items.question: How is the Shiva principle understood as threefold in its aspects?
premises: The Shiva principle can be considered
It becomes threefold
These aspects include pure, timeless, and kala-related modes
items.inference: The Shiva principle, become threefold, is understood through the aspects of pure, timeless, kala, and akala.
uncertainties: The internal parsing of svacchākālakalākale is doctrinally nuanced
items.plain_english: In the Shiva principle, become threefold, as pure, timeless, kala, and akala.

rows.grounds: the potency or energy of knowledge

items.question: What characterizes competence as undivided vigor of knowledge?
premises: Competence can be present
It can be undivided
The vigor of knowledge operates constantly
items.inference: In competence, undivided capability is constantly the vigor of knowledge.
uncertainties: satate may be read as an indeclinable or a verbal form in some contexts
items.plain_english: In competence there is undivided competence, constantly as the vigor of knowledge.

rows.grounds: from absorption in the sense of mine

items.question: How does immersion in mine-ness toward objects create a new world?
premises: Knowable objects can be appropriated as mine
Immersion in mine-ness can occur
A new world can be fashioned
items.inference: From immersion in mine-ness toward the object of knowledge, one creates a new world.
uncertainties: The agent of nirmiṇoti is implied by context
items.plain_english: From immersion in mine-ness toward the object, one creates a new world.

rows.grounds: the state of having all desires fulfilled
the presence or functioning of all seasons

items.question: What powers of desire and time arise in the state of affection?
premises: Affection can be a locus of experience
All-desire-ness can manifest
Time can present all seasons
items.inference: In affection, there is all-desire-ness and, through time, the turning of all seasons.
uncertainties: The causal relation between kālāt and sarvartuvartanam is compactly expressed
items.plain_english: But in affection there is all-desire-ness, and from time the turning of all seasons.

rows.grounds: of one's own self; sandhi: sva + ātmanaḥ
for or indeed; sandhi form of hi
sovereignty or splendor without limiting conditions

items.question: What kind of glory belongs to one's own self without obstruction or conditions?
premises: One's own self possesses glory
Its purposes are unobstructed
This glory is without limiting conditions
items.inference: The glory of one's own self is unobstructed in purpose and free from limiting conditions.
uncertainties: nirupādhi may imply absence of external supports or absence of limiting attributes
items.plain_english: Indeed, the glory of one's own self is unobstructed in purpose and without limiting conditions.
